decision.reason: Retain existing model: Terra was faster in this small sample but cost about five times as much and did not consistently improve experiment suitability. No model-wide superiority claim.

productGuards: SHA-256 binds stored observation to original code, probe id/expression, runner version; stale/missing records require rerun before quota or AI.
Server-only fixed original outputs are checked against all 12 actual QuickJS base/transfer executions; incompatible reported output is rejected before quota or AI, even with a matching source hash.
Stored starter must match the canonical curriculum before applying expected output. Submitted current code is never executed on server.
Late coaching cannot attach after prediction, observation, or source changes; newer edits and notes are preserved.

finalFocusedRecheck.scope: coaching API and mobile legacy observation on Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; overlaps initial 18, not 24 distinct scenarios

limitations: A source hash and known-output match cannot prove that a client executed anything, and cannot certify understanding.
Direct provider diagnostics intentionally bypass HTTP preflight; the inconsistent-output case is now rejected by the product API.
Contract was added after baseline, so payloads/source hashes are not identical across revisions.
AI experiments remain prose, may need insertion into the shown probe or an async wrapper, and are not independently executed or guaranteed valid.
No unseen test set, independent human ratings, matched competitor comparison, real learner transfer study, or production deployment.
